Clothing and the couch have a fuzzy fiber shader (visible matted texture on the man's black coat and the woman's rust turtleneck) while the skin on both noses/faces is smooth matte CG with no fiber detail and no fingerprints, tool marks, or armature seams anywhere in frame. Across the ~1s-spaced periodic frames, expression and hand poses progress continuously rather than in discrete snapped steps, which is more consistent with a rigged CG puppet than a hand-manipulated clay/felt puppet. Flagging uncertainty: sampling is too sparse (~1 frame/sec against 30fps source) to confirm whether the underlying render was done on 1s/2s holds or at full frame rate.

The periodic keyframes are spaced roughly 1 second apart, too coarse to directly judge sub-second holds, but the poses sampled show continuously different, non-repeating expressions and hand positions at every step (no two consecutive periodic frames are identical except the final end-card), implying the underlying animation is not resting on long multi-second static holds.
